national_indicator_definition: This indicator measures total antibiotic consumption in human medicine in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Consumption is expressed as the number of defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). The indicator enables monitoring of antibiotic consumption and changes in their use over time.
national_rationale: The data source is the World Health Organization (WHO), through the Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS), which includes the collection of data on antimicrobial consumption (GLASS-AMU). The data are based on aggregated administrative data on antibiotic consumption, collected from available national sources and submitted to WHO. Consumption is expressed in defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID), in accordance with WHO methodology. Progress is calculated automatically based on changes in the indicator values over time. Since a reduction in antibiotic consumption is the desired direction, a decrease in the indicator value represents progress, while an increase represents deterioration. The displayed progress status reflects the trend in the indicator and does not constitute an assessment against a formally established national target.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers antibiotic consumption in human medicine, in accordance with the WHO GLASS-AMU methodology. Under this methodology, the data cover antibiotics belonging to ATC group J01, as well as certain medicines from ATC groups A07AA and P01AB, subject to specified exclusions. Consumption is expressed in defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). The data enable monitoring of antibiotic consumption over time.
national_long_objective: The rational use of antibiotics and the reduction of their unnecessary and inappropriate consumption are important activities in combating antimicrobial resistance in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Monitoring antibiotic consumption enables changes in their use to be assessed and provides a basis for planning measures aimed at improving their rational use. Based on the available information, no officially adopted quantified national target has been established for this indicator.
eu_indicator_definition: This indicator measures total antibiotic consumption in human medicine in both the community and hospital sectors. Consumption is expressed as the number of defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). At the European Union level, the indicator covers antibacterials for systemic use belonging to ATC group J01.
eu_rationale: The data source is the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), through the European Surveillance of Antimicrobial Consumption Network (ESAC-Net). Data are collected annually and cover antibiotic consumption in both the community and hospital sectors. Consumption is expressed in defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID), in accordance with the World Health Organization's ATC/DDD methodology. The European Union aggregate represents a population-weighted mean, with imputation and adjustment procedures applied where necessary to address missing data.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers antibacterials for systemic use belonging to ATC group J01, used in human medicine in both the community and hospital sectors. Expressing consumption in DDD per 1,000 inhabitants per day enables monitoring of changes over time and comparison between countries applying harmonised data collection and processing methodologies. Data are available annually.
eu_long_objective: Reducing unnecessary and inappropriate antibiotic use is an important element of efforts to combat antimicrobial resistance in the European Union. The 2023 Council Recommendation on stepping up EU actions to combat antimicrobial resistance sets a target of reducing total antibiotic consumption in human medicine by 20% by 2030, compared with 2019. This target applies to the population-weighted consumption at the European Union level.
